verses.text: Then the people of Israel moved on and camped in the plains of Moab, along the Jordan River across from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites.
The people of Moab were terrified because there were so many Israelites. Moab was filled with dread because of the people of Israel.
So the Moabites said to the leaders of Midian, "This crowd is going to eat up everything around us, like an ox eats up the grass in a field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to call Balaam son of Beor, who lived at Pethor near the Euphrates River, in his own native land. Balak's message said, "A whole nation has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the land, and they have settled next to me.

Please come now and put a curse on these people for me, because they are too strong for me. Then perhaps I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed."
The leaders of Moab and Midian set out, taking with them the payment for a fortune-teller. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak's message.
Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back whatever answer the LORD gives me." So the Moabite leaders stayed with him.
God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:
'A nation has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Then perhaps I will be able to fight them and drive them away.'"
But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not put a curse on these people, because they are blessed."
The next morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's leaders, "Go back to your own country, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the Moabite leaders went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
Then Balak sent other leaders, more of them and more important than the first.
They came to Balaam and said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: 'Please do not let anything stop you from coming to me.
I will reward you very richly and do whatever you say. Please come and put a curse on these people for me.'"
But Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his palace full of silver and gold, I could not do anything, big or small, that goes against the command of the LORD my God.
Now stay here tonight as the others did, so I can find out what else the LORD will tell me."
That night God came to Balaam and said, "Since these men have come to call you, go with them. But do only what I tell you."
So Balaam got up in the morning, put the saddle on his donkey, and went with the Moabite leaders.
But God was angry that he was going, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to block his way. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand, she turned off the road into a field. Balaam beat her to make her go back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between two vineyards, with a wall on each side.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed close to the wall, crushing Balaam's foot against it. So he beat her again.
Then the angel of the LORD went ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. He became furious and beat her with his stick.
Then the LORD made the donkey able to speak, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have beaten me these three times?"
Balaam answered the donkey, "You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your own donkey, which you have always ridden, right up to this day? Have I ever done this to you before?" "No," he said.
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a sword in his hand. So Balaam bowed low with his face to the ground.
The angel of the LORD asked him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I came to block your way, because the path you are on is wrong in my sight.
The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, I would certainly have killed you by now, but I would have let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know you were standing in the road to stop me. Now, if you are not pleased, I will go back home."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but say only what I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's leaders.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite town on the Arnon River, at the edge of his land.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send you an urgent message to come? Why didn't you come to me? Do you think I am not able to reward you well?"
Balaam answered Balak, "Well, I have come to you now. But do I have the power to say just anything? I must say only what God puts in my mouth."
Then Balaam went with Balak to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balak offered cattle and sheep as sacrifices, and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the leaders who were with him.
The next morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal, the high places of Baal. From there Balaam could see part of the people of Israel.
